paragraphs.text: The kākāpō is a large, flightless parrot found only in New Zealand. It is nocturnal, feeding at night on plants, seeds and fruit, and it can live for more than 60 years. Because it evolved without mammal predators, it defends itself by freezing when threatened, a strategy that was useless against the cats and rats brought by European settlers. By 1995, only 51 birds remained. Today, every kākāpō lives on predator-free islands and is monitored by a radio transmitter, and the population has recovered to more than 240.
